clue.text: Lack the encouragement of love?

parts.note: plays on the proverb that being apart makes the heart grow fonder: the lack of someone's presence is what encourages love

explanation.surface: A lonely heart complains that nobody ever spurs on their romance.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is 'absence makes the heart grow fonder', so the thing that is a lack yet feeds love is being away.
explanation.definitionFit: Being away from someone is a lack of their company, and the proverb says that lack feeds affection.

clue.text: Got together, the same sad characters

indicators.note: characters means the letters of same sad are taken as loose characters to rearrange

explanation.surface: The same miserable people gathered once again.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to gather or collect a quantity of something.

clue.text: Flattery works in domestic melodrama

parts.note: soap is slang for flattery, as in soft soap
opera is the plural of opus, a work

explanation.surface: Buttering up succeeds in a family drama.
explanation.walkthrough: OPERA is the Latin plural of opus, so it means works.
explanation.definitionFit: A serial drama about everyday family life, originally sponsored by detergent makers.

clue.text: Moment with nobody round about

indicators.note: round says the word for nobody goes round the abbreviation for about

parts.note: none means not one person, nobody
c, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: An instant with no one nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: The present occasion or time being, as in 'for the nonce'.

clue.text: Heart-breaking job — fortification needed

indicators.note: breaking means the letters of heart are smashed apart and rearranged

parts.note: work means a job

explanation.surface: A heartbreaking task: a fort is required.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heart-breaking' looks like one adjective, but 'breaking' rearranges HEART into EARTH.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank of soil raised as a defensive rampart.

clue.text: Little girl's carried away (with a difference)

parts.note: Di is a short girl's name, with the possessive s kept
sent, as in 'that music really sent me', means enraptured

explanation.surface: A small child has been swept off by some enthusiasm, though in an odd way.
explanation.walkthrough: '(with a difference)' looks like an aside, but 'difference' is the definition, in its sense of a disagreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A difference of opinion is a disagreement, the same as an objection to the majority view.

clue.text: Daughter split with the tenor

parts.note: a rift is a split

explanation.surface: A daughter has broken up with the tenor singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tenor' looks like the singer but means general gist, as in the tenor of a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: The drift of an argument is its general meaning or gist.

clue.text: Confirmed bore

explanation.surface: A chronic bore.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge sustains, or upholds, an objection; and a beam that bore a load supported it.

clue.text: Under age to provide the inspiration for Catullus

indicators.note: in a down entry the word to is placed under the word for age

parts.note: an era is an age

explanation.surface: Someone too young to be a source of inspiration for a Roman poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under age' looks like too young, but tells you TO goes beneath ERA. Catullus was a Roman love poet.
explanation.definitionFit: The Muse of love poetry, who would have inspired a Roman love poet.

clue.text: Theatre changed on that account

indicators.note: changed signals the letters of theatre being altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A playhouse was altered for that reason.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic adverb meaning because of that, or thereupon.

clue.text: A chief in great haste

parts.note: main means principal or chief, as in the main reason

explanation.surface: A leader rushes about at top speed.
explanation.definitionFit: An old poetic adverb meaning with full force, hence at full speed or in a hurry.

clue.text: Check condition and put back

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain, so a rein is a check
state means condition, as in a state of repair

explanation.surface: Inspect something's condition and then return it to its place.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore someone or something to a former position is to put it back there.

clue.text: The way I talk with a bird

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
the numeral I is one
chat means talk

explanation.surface: Someone explains their manner of speaking alongside a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The way I talk' reads as someone describing their accent; 'way' is a street and 'I' the Roman numeral for a single unit. 'The' and 'with a' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A small songbird of heaths and moors, named for its call like two stones knocked together.

clue.text: Previously a look out

parts.note: fore is the golfer's shout warning people to look out for the ball

explanation.surface: Someone recalls that earlier there was a lookout posted.
explanation.walkthrough: FORE is the warning cry golfers shout to anyone in the path of a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for before or earlier, as in sailors' 'afore the mast'.

clue.text: Nighted like Keats's December

parts.note: recalls the opening of a Keats poem, 'In a ...-nighted December', so the missing word is the one that precedes the hyphen

explanation.surface: A quiz question about how the poet Keats described the winter nights.
explanation.walkthrough: Keats's poem begins 'In a drear-nighted December'; the clue asks for the word that goes before 'nighted'.
explanation.definitionFit: The poetic adjective meaning dismal or gloomy, which Keats joins to 'nighted' for his bleak winter.

clue.text: Forgiving about a letter

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a missive is a letter

explanation.surface: Someone feels forgiving about a letter they got.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to remission, the pardoning of sins or debts.

clue.text: Near to being in public from one day to the next

definitions.text: from one day to the next

indicators.note: being in says the word for near sits inside the word for public

parts.note: overt means open, done in public
nigh means near

explanation.surface: Someone is nearly famous within a day.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lasting through the night lasts from one evening into the next morning.

clue.text: Rows between auditors in an advanced state

indicators.note: between says the rows go inside the word for auditors

parts.note: ears are what listen, so auditors
lines are rows

explanation.surface: Arguments among accountants have got well along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rows' looks like quarrels and 'auditors' like accountants; they are LINES and EARS (listeners).
explanation.definitionFit: Being early means being ahead of time, as crops are forward in season.

clue.text: Simpleton to pay for this plant

parts.note: a goose is a silly person
to foot the bill is to pay it

explanation.surface: A fool is made to pay for a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A weed of the beet family, named for its leaves shaped like a webbed foot.

clue.text: He helps to get girls tight, and takes Mary out

definitions.text: He helps to get girls tight

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of takes and Mary are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A man gets women drunk and takes one of them out on a date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tight' suggests drunk, but means laced into a corset; stays are corset stiffeners. 'out' rearranges TAKES MARY.
explanation.definitionFit: A maker of stays, the stiffened corsets that pulled wearers into a narrow waist.

clue.text: Comforted — and thus inspirited!

parts.note: so means thus
laced means spiked with spirits, as coffee laced with brandy

explanation.surface: Cheered up, and so given new heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspirited' means encouraged, but here a drink laced with spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Consoled in distress.

clue.text: Forced bird out of the river

indicators.note: the bird is placed out round the river, enclosing it

parts.note: a dove is a bird
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A bird was made to leave the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Drove is the past tense of drive, to push or compel someone along.

clue.text: He may make his mark as note reader

parts.note: E is a musical note
a lector is a reader, as in church

explanation.surface: A man who reads notes aloud may leave his signature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make his mark' reads as becoming famous; it is the cross a voter puts on a ballot paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A voter makes a mark on the ballot paper.

clue.text: Place where grasshopper comes to premature end

indicators.note: the insect's name ends early, losing its final letter

parts.note: a locust is a kind of grasshopper

explanation.surface: Someone asks where a grasshopper died young.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word for place, used in English for a site or position.

clue.text: Clear direction in class

indicators.note: in places the direction inside the word for class

parts.note: a clan is a group or class
E is east, a compass direction

explanation.surface: Clear instructions given in a lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: Clean means free of obstruction or blame, unmarked.

clue.text: Shadow man, by design, at the chapter's end

parts.note: to tail someone is to shadow or follow them
a piece is a man in chess or draughts

explanation.surface: A secret agent tails a suspect deliberately until the chapter closes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shadow man' reads as a spy; in fact a man in chess is a PIECE. 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A small decorative engraving printed in the space at the end of a chapter.

clue.text: Author, half dry, is on the wagon

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece sits on top of the second
half means only the first of the two letters for teetotal is kept

parts.note: TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol, dry
a wain is a wagon

explanation.surface: A writer, partly sober, has given up drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the wagon' looks like teetotal but is WAIN. Mark Twain is the American author.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain, the pen name of the American writer Samuel Clemens.

clue.text: Old Bob invested in top prize for hymn

indicators.note: invested in places the shilling inside the word for top prize

parts.note: the palm is the prize of victory
a bob was the British slang for an old shilling, abbreviated s

explanation.surface: Old Bob put money into a top award for church music.
explanation.walkthrough: A bob was a shilling in old British money, written s.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacred song from the biblical Book of that name.

clue.text: Rattle — make a fuss about mine

indicators.note: about says the word for making a fuss goes round the word for mine

parts.note: to create is British slang for kicking up a fuss
a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: Someone is told to kick up a stink over a colliery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Create' is British informal for making a fuss ('don't create').
explanation.definitionFit: To crackle or make a rapid series of small sharp noises, like a crackling fire.

clue.text: A fit, more or less

parts.note: a bout is a fit or attack, as of coughing

explanation.surface: A garment fits roughly.
explanation.definitionFit: Approximately, as in 'about ten people came'.

clue.text: Churchman, holding a biblical work, is austere

indicators.note: holding says the churchman contains the other pieces

parts.note: a dean is a senior clergyman
NT is the New Testament

explanation.surface: A clergyman clutching a Bible has a stern manner.
explanation.definitionFit: In the manner of the poet of the Inferno, whose vision is grim and severe.

clue.text: Puts me right? Wrong, old horse

indicators.note: wrong means the letters of puts me are set out incorrectly

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be corrected, only to be told they are wrong about an old horse.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for a packhorse or the driver of one.
